A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, theoretical framework, and core experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on compressibility, adversarial robustness, transfer learning, universal perturbations, and pruning, including additional empirical analyses in Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds transformer and CLIP experiments, attack-budget sensitivity results, and post-pruning fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The compression-inducing interventions, epsilon-based global pruning, and variance regularization of the top 5% of filter norms remain unchanged. v2 applies these ideas to additional architectures and experimental pipelines without introducing a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds Flickr30k fine-tuning and ImageNet-1k zero-shot classification with CLIP, extending coverage beyond the image-classification datasets and tasks in v1. MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN remain covered.

E2.justification: Matched retained experiments preserve their unregularized/compressible controls and layerwise/global pruning comparisons. The transformer experiments extend these controlled comparisons; no additional competing compression or defense algorithm is benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 introduces ViT/Swin training and fine-tuning settings, CLIP top-5 zero-shot evaluation, attack-budget and adversarial-training-mixture sweeps, and post-pruning adversarial fine-tuning. Appendix C.3 also newly specifies 10% adversarial validation, conflicting with the retained 5% general rule; an actual split change cannot be established.

E4.justification: v2 adds attack-budget/training-mixture sensitivity (Table 1), loss-gap checks (Table 4), and post-pruning fine-tuning analysis (Figure 16). The row-sparse adversarial fine-tuning study in v1 Figure 4(left) is removed, while the spectral counterpart remains in v2 Figure 11(left).

E5.justification: Both versions report at least three seeds for main results, ten seeds for the matrix-norm experiment, and one-standard-deviation error bars for the group-lasso analysis. No changed replication count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds transformer/CLIP curves and Tables 1–4. For example, its new Swin/SVHN sweep reports robust accuracy of 0.384 at alpha=0 versus 0.083 at alpha=0.1, with standard accuracy 0.889 versus 0.875. It also newly quantifies bound–gap correlation as 0.947 and adds post-pruning results; most matched earlier plots retain their results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.2 introduces Theorem B.4 and proofs of neuron- and spectral-compressibility lower bounds on operator norms, complementing the retained upper bounds. The spread definition is relocated rather than newly introduced. The spectral lower bound's square root requires a domain restriction that is not explicitly stated.

C1.justification: The central compressibility–vulnerability claims remain. Contribution 2 explicitly extends empirical applicability to modern encoders, while contribution 4 shifts emphasis from proposing regularization/pruning strategies to practical compression implications and promising directions.

C2.justification: v2 recommends combining moderate pruning or low-rank approximation with quantization or distillation and adds a floor-effect rationale for reduced attack budgets. Its claim of compression-pattern independence across budgets exceeds Table 1's direct comparison, which varies adversarial training mixture rather than compressibility. The global-Lipschitz limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with a concrete repository link and documents transformer checkpoints, patch sizes, CLIP training settings, and seven text-prompt templates. Conversely, it omits v1's alpha=0.01 specification for the retained global-pruning example. Repository availability itself was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting transformers, CLIP, new datasets and software, and sparse local-Lipschitz predictors. Kuzmin et al. and Hong et al. support the new discussion of combining compression approaches. The existing related-work narrative and central research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and explanations, moves the detailed spread discussion into Appendix B.1, reorders experimental discussion, and divides Appendix C into numbered subsections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory schematic, transformer and post-pruning plots, and four tables. It redisplays an existing appendix bound plot as main-text Figure 3 and combines earlier panels into Figure 7. Figure 7's caption reverses the descriptions of its two central panels.

improvement.justification: The transformer/CLIP and post-pruning studies strengthen practical applicability, while additional setup information and a concrete code link improve reproducibility. These gains are qualified by conflicting validation fractions, Table 2 ratios that do not match the displayed accuracies, overinterpretation of the budget experiment, and the missing domain qualification in the new lower bound. Overall quality improves, but the new evidence and documentation need correction.
